fique: 'Biggest of the world' → biggest in the world

p: Is Rio bigger than São Paulo?
Who is older, you or your brother?
Is coffee better than tea?
What is the biggest room in your house?
Who is the tallest person in your family?
Is your city hotter than Curitiba?
t: Meu irmão é mais alto que eu.
My brother is taller than me.
Esse é o melhor restaurante da cidade.
This is the best restaurant in the city.
O inglês é mais fácil que o alemão.
Hoje está mais frio que ontem.
Ela é a pessoa mais engraçada que eu conheço.
She is the funniest person I know.
c: A car is ___ (fast) than a bike.
This book is ___ (interesting) than the movie.
r: My car is more big than yours.
My car is bigger than yours.

p: Compare your city and another city you know.
What is the most beautiful place you've visited?
Is life easier now than 20 years ago? Why?
Who is the most patient person you know?
What is the worst job in the world, in your opinion?
Is it better to live in a house or an apartment?
t: Essa casa não é tão grande quanto a outra.
This house isn't as big as the other one.
Quanto mais eu estudo, mais eu aprendo.
The more I study, the more I learn.
O trânsito está cada vez pior.
The traffic is getting worse and worse.
Ele é muito mais velho do que parece.
He is much older than he looks.
Qual é o lugar mais bonito do Brasil?
What is the most beautiful place in Brazil?
c: This is ___ (far) I have ever walked.
Rio is one of the ___ (beautiful) cities in the world.
r: My house is smaller than your house. (as...as)
My house isn't as big as yours.

p: Is it better to have a well-paid job or an interesting job?
What was the hardest year of your life? Why?
Compare living in Brazil and living abroad.
Which is more important: talent or effort?
What's the most useful thing you've ever learned?
Is it getting easier or harder to buy a house? Why?
t: Esse foi de longe o pior filme que eu já vi.
That was by far the worst movie I've ever seen.
Ela é bem menos tímida do que antes.
She is much less shy than before.
Não é tão caro quanto eu imaginava.
It's not as expensive as I thought.
c: The new phone is twice ___ expensive ___ the old one.
It was the ___ (bad) day of my life.
r: The traffic gets worse every year.
The traffic is getting worse and worse.
If you study more, you learn more.
The more you study, the more you learn.
This phone costs double the price of that one.
This phone is twice as expensive as that one.

fala: Compare three cities, jobs or restaurants you know.
Debate: city life vs country life.
Talk about the best and worst things in your year.
Compare yourself now and 10 years ago.
escrita: Write 6 comparisons between two places you know.
Write about the best, worst and most interesting things in your city.

topicos.nome: Modal verbs: should / must / have to
fique: 'You should to go' → You should go

p: Should I drink more water?
Do you have to work on Saturdays?
What should I visit in your city?
Do you have to wear a uniform?
Should children use phones?
What time do you have to wake up?
c: You ___ (não deveria) eat so much sugar.
r: You should to go to the doctor.
You should go to the doctor.
It's a good idea to study.

p: What should people do to learn English faster?
What do you have to do at work that you don't like?
What rules do you have to follow at your job?
What should a tourist never do in Rio?
What didn't you have to do as a child that children have to do now?
What should the government do about traffic?
t: Você não pode usar o celular durante a prova.
You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
Eu tive que esperar duas horas.
I had to wait two hours.
Do we have to leave at seven?
r: You mustn't come if you don't want. (não é proibido)
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
It's my advice: don't buy that car.

p: What should schools teach that they don't teach now?
What do you think everyone must do at least once in their life?
What rules should companies have about working from home?
What did you have to give up to get where you are?
Should social media be banned for children? Why?
What's something you feel you should do but never do?
t: Eu não tinha que ir, mas fui mesmo assim.
I didn't have to go, but I went anyway.
Você precisa ver esse filme! (recomendação forte)
You didn't have to bring anything.
Será que eu deveria aceitar a proposta?
c: You ___ (precisa) try this restaurant! It's amazing.
We ___ (vamos ter que) work on Saturday.
She ___ (não precisou) pay for the ticket.
r: It was a mistake not to tell me.
It's not necessary to bring food.
You don't have to bring food.

fala: Give advice to a friend who wants to lose weight / find a job / learn English.
Explain the rules of your workplace or a sport.
Talk about obligations you had as a teenager.
Debate: should work weeks be 4 days?
escrita: Write 5 pieces of advice for a tourist in Rio.
Write 5 rules for your house or office (must/mustn't/have to).
Write 3 things you should have done differently.

fique: Adjetivo depois do substantivo: 'a house big' → a big house
Adjetivo no plural: 'beautifuls places' → beautiful places
What is she like? (personalidade) vs What does she look like? (aparência)

p: Does your mother have long or short hair?
Is your city quiet or noisy?
Are you more like your mother or your father?
Is your street beautiful?
What color are your eyes?
Is your best friend tall or short?
t: Ela tem cabelo curto e olhos castanhos.
She has short hair and brown eyes.
Minha cidade é grande e barulhenta.
My city is big and noisy.
É uma casa pequena e bonita.
r: I live in a house big.
I live in a big house.

p: What is your best friend like?
What does your boss look like?
Describe your neighborhood. What do you like about it?
Describe the most beautiful place you've visited.
Who in your family has the strongest personality?
What is your favorite room like?
t: Meu bairro é tranquilo, mas não tem muito para fazer.
My neighborhood is quiet, but there isn't much to do.
Ela tem uns quarenta e poucos anos.
c: What ___ your new boss like? He's very organized.
What does she ___ like? She's tall with curly hair.

p: Describe someone who had a big influence on you.
Describe your city to someone who has never been to Brazil.
What personality traits do you admire? Which ones annoy you?
Describe a place you'd love to live in and why.
How would your friends describe you?
Describe a typical Brazilian, avoiding stereotypes.
t: Ele é o tipo de pessoa que ajuda todo mundo.
He's the kind of person who helps everyone.
Apesar de ser tímida, ela fala muito bem em público.
Although she's shy, she speaks very well in public.
É um bairro animado, cheio de bares e restaurantes.
It's a lively neighborhood, full of bars and restaurants.
Ele tem um senso de humor meio estranho.
He has a slightly weird sense of humor.
A vista de lá de cima é de tirar o fôlego.
The view from up there is breathtaking.
c: The town is ___ (cheia de) tourists in summer.
My grandmother was a ___ (forte, independente) woman.
r: He is a person that helps all people.
He's the kind of person who helps everyone.
The neighborhood has many bars, it's very animated.
The neighborhood has many bars; it's very lively.
She is very sympathetic with everyone. (= simpática)
She is very friendly / nice to everyone.

fala: Describe a family member: appearance and personality.
Describe your city to a tourist in 2 minutes.
Describe a person — I guess who it is (famous person).
Describe your dream house.
escrita: Describe your best friend (6 sentences: appearance + personality).
Describe your neighborhood for a travel blog.
Describe a place from your childhood.

fique: 'Many money' → much money / a lot of money

p: Is there any milk in your fridge?
Do you drink much water?
How many brothers and sisters do you have?
Do you have any pets?
How much coffee do you drink a day?
Are there many cars on your street?
c: There is ___ water in the bottle.
How ___ books do you read a year?
r: I have a lot of money.

p: How much time do you spend on your phone every day?
What food do you always have at home?
How many hours do you sleep?
Do you need any information about my city?
How much luggage do you take on a trip?
Is there any advice you'd give to a new student?
t: Você pode me dar um conselho?
Can you give me some advice?
Não tenho muito dinheiro, mas tenho muitos amigos.
I don't have much money, but I have a lot of friends.
c: Can I have ___ (um pouco de) water?
r: She gave me a good advice.
She gave me some good advice / a good piece of advice.

p: Do you think people today have less free time than before?
How much money is enough to be happy?
Is there any news that surprised you recently?
Do you have enough time for your hobbies?
What do you have too much of? What do you have too little of?
How much experience do you need to be a good teacher?
t: There are very few places like this.
Tenho pouco tempo, mas o suficiente.
I have a little time, but enough.
Não tem nenhuma notícia boa hoje.
How much luggage are you taking?
Ele tem experiência demais para essa vaga.
He has too much experience for this position.
c: I have ___ (amigos demais) on social media.
r: I don't have any free time — use no.

fala: Plan a party: what and how much do we need to buy?
Describe what is in your fridge right now.
Talk about what you have too much/too little of in your life.
Role-play at a market: ask prices and quantities.
escrita: Write a shopping list with quantities (some, a few, a lot of).
Write 5 sentences about your city with much/many/a lot of.

fique: 'I have went' → I have gone / I went
Com tempo definido: 'I have seen him yesterday' → I saw him yesterday

p: Have you ever been to Argentina?
Have you ever eaten sushi?
Have you ever seen snow?
Have you finished your homework?
Have you ever lost your phone?
Have you ever met a famous person?
t: Have you ever seen this movie?
r: Have you ever seen this movie?

p: What countries have you visited?
Have you ever had a really bad job? Tell me about it.
What is something you've never done but want to do?
Have you done anything interesting this week?
Have you already planned your next vacation?
Have you ever changed your mind about something important?
t: Have you answered the email yet?
Eu já fui lá duas vezes.
r: I have visited Rome last year.
She has finished already the report.
She has already finished the report.

p: What's the most interesting place you've ever been to? When did you go?
What's the best decision you've ever made?
Have you ever had to speak English in a real situation? What happened?
What have you learned this year?
Have you ever done something you regret? What happened?
What's changed in your city since you were a child?
t: É a primeira vez que eu como isso.
It's the first time I've eaten this.
Já faz tempo que não nos vemos.
We haven't seen each other for a long time.
Você já se perguntou por quê?
Ela foi para a Europa e ainda não voltou. (gone)
She has gone to Europe and hasn't come back yet.
A lot has changed since then.
c: It's the first time I ___ (eat) here.
She's not here. She has ___ (go) to the bank.
I've ___ (be) to the bank. I'm back.
How many times have you ___ (fly) this year?
r: Is the first time I eat this.
It's the first time I've eaten this.
She has been to Europe. (ainda está lá)
I haven't seen you since much time.
I haven't seen you for a long time.
